extracted.intended_audience: Applicants entering the European phase via the PCT (Euro‑PCT applicants), and their patent attorneys/representatives
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements, time limits and fees that apply when an international (PCT) application enters the European phase before the EPO, including searches, examinations, priority issues, translations, fee payments and remedies for missed acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: 30% reduction in examination fee for admissible non‑EPO language filers
rubrics_metrics.description: A 30% reduction in the examination fee is available to SMEs, natural persons, non-profit organizations, universities or public research organizations having their residence or principal place of business in a EPC contracting state with an official language other than English, French or German if they file the request for examination in an official language of that state (“admissible non‑EPO language”) and declare themselves to be entitled to do so (EPC Rule 6(6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request for examination may be filed up until the examination fee is paid. If the request for examination in an admissible non‑EPO language is filed subsequently, it must be accompanied by a translation of the request for examination in the procedural language. (See Annex EP.II, EPO Form 1200, page 2, box 4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined reductions and refund of examination fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If the conditions for both reductions are fulfilled, the examination fee is first reduced by 75% and the 30% reduction is applied to the resulting total, giving a total reduction of 82.50%. The examination fee is refunded in full if the application is withdrawn, refused or deemed to be withdrawn before substantive examination has begun. Fifty percent of the examination fee is refunded if withdrawal/refusal/deemed withdrawal occurs after substantive examination has begun but before the expiry of the time limit for replying to the first invitation under Article 94(3) EPC (or before the Rule 71(3) communication date if no such invitation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deemed withdrawal for non‑fulfilment of certain formal requirements (EPC Rule 160)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the translation of the international application or the request for examination is not filed in due time or if the filing fee (including additional pages), search fee, examination fee or designation fee is not paid in due time, the European patent application is deemed withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant will be informed of the deemed withdrawal and EPC Rule 112(2) applies. Loss of rights is deemed not to have occurred if, within two months of the EPO notification, further processing is requested by payment of the respective fee(s) for further processing and the omitted act is completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further processing when request for examination and/or examination fee late
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant neither filed the request for examination nor paid the examination fee in due time, further processing must be requested in respect of both omissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant must file the request for examination and pay the examination fee together with two fees for further processing: a flat fee for further processing in respect of the request for examination and 50% of the examination fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary European search requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: As a rule, a supplementary European search must be performed for each international application entering the European phase and a search fee must be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The supplementary search is based on the last set of (amended) claims available to the EPO on the date of expiry of the time limit set under EPC Rule 161(2). If the request for examination was filed before transmittal of the supplementary European search report, the EPO invites the applicant, after transmittal, to indicate whether he wishes to proceed further with the application. The applicant may waive the right to receive such communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to reply to a negative search opinion (EPC Rule 70a(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant is required to reply to a search opinion within the time limit set by the EPO in its communication under EPC Rule 70a(2) if the EPO has issued a negative written opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Guidelines for Examination in the EPO, B‑XI, 8 and EP.18 for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispensation from supplementary search when EPO acted as (S)ISA
rubrics_metrics.description: No supplementary European search is performed and no search fee is payable if the international search report (or supplementary international search report) was established by the EPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In that case the applicant will be invited to comment on the written opinion of the ISA or on the IPRP (Chapter II), or on the supplementary international search report and to amend the application within six months from notification of the invitation (EPC Rule 161(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Search fee payment, reductions and possible refunds (EP.16b)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a supplementary European search report is to be established, the search fee must be paid within the 31‑month time limit and may be reduced by EUR 1,185 where the international search report was drawn up by specified Offices. If the application claims priority of an earlier application for which a search was carried out by the EPO, (a part of) the fee paid for the supplementary European search may be refunded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The level of any refund depends on the type of the earlier search and the extent to which the EPO benefits from the earlier search report when carrying out the supplementary search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing requirements (EP.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Standard‑compliant sequence listing in TXT format is contained in the international application under PCT Rule 5.2 and is furnished to or accessible by the EPO, the applicant does not have to submit it again in TXT format when entering the regional phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a TXT listing is not available on expiry of the period under Rule 159(1) EPC, the applicant will be invited to file it within a non‑extendable period of two months and to pay the late furnishing fee. The late filing must be accompanied by a declaration that the sequence listing does not extend beyond the content of the application as originally filed. Filing on paper/PDF is not required; if filed on paper/PDF a statement of identity with the electronic form is required. Deficiencies not remedied lead to refusal (EPC Rule 30(3)). For applications filed on or after 1 July 2022 the applicable standard is WIPO ST.26.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and time limits (EP.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may always file voluntary amendments within the 31‑month time limit, and further amendments until expiry of the time limit set in the combined communication under EPC Rules 161 and 162. Mandatory amendments/comments must be filed within the time limit set in that communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The communication under EPC Rules 161 and 162 is issued promptly once the application has entered the European phase and (provided the ISR is available) sets a six‑month non‑extendable time limit. The applicant can waive the Rule 161/162 communication via Form 1200 under specified conditions. Amendments may in no circumstances go beyond the disclosure in the international application as filed. Whenever amendments are filed the applicant must identify them and indicate their basis; failure to do so may lead to a one‑month non‑extendable correction request and, if not remedied, deemed withdrawal (EPC Article 94(4)). Amendments after certain stages require examining division consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant procedure and implication of performing requested acts (EP.19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to the decision to grant the European patent the applicant receives a communication containing the text in which the Examining Division intends to grant and an invitation to pay the grant and printing fees and to supply translations of the claims in the two other official languages of the EPO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance of these acts implies approval of the text. The communication may also include an invitation to pay additional claims fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment deadline for grant/printing/claims fees (EP.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: The amounts of the fees for grant, printing and claims are indicated in Annex EP.I and must be paid within four months from the communication pursuant to EPC Rule 71(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of claims on grant (EP.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the same period for payment of the grant fee the claims must be translated into the two official languages of the EPO which are not the language of proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See paragraphs EP.02 and EP.19 for language rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early processing request (EP.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant wishes processing and examination to start earlier than expiry of the PCT time limits, he must file an express request for early processing by ticking the checkbox in section 12.1 of EPO Form 1200.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant must fulfill the requirements for entry into the European phase as if the 31‑month time limit expired on the date he requests early processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPO review under PCT Article 25 (EP.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: At the applicant's request the EPO may review whether a refusal by the receiving Office to accord a filing date, a declaration that a Euro‑PCT application is withdrawn, or an IB finding under PCT Article 12(3) is the result of an error or omission, in which case the Euro‑PCT application can proceed as a European application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To obtain such review applicants must, within the two‑month time limit under PCT Rule 51.1, request the IB to send copies promptly to the EPO, pay the filing fee under EPC Rule 159(1)(c) and, where required, furnish a translation within the same two‑month time limit. Applicants are recommended to undertake remaining steps for entry to the European phase simultaneously. If the EPO denies error/omission a notice of appeal may be lodged within two months (fee payable) and grounds filed within four months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further processing (EP.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: Further processing may be requested where the applicant has missed a time limit during the international or national phase and further processing is not ruled out under Rule 135(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must be made by completing the omitted act(s) and paying the fee(s) for further processing (amounts in Annex EP.I) within two months of notification of noting of loss of rights (EPC Rule 112(1)). The fee for further processing varies depending on whether the loss of rights occurred due to an omitted act (flat rate) or late payment (50% of that fee). In some cases both fees must be paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re‑establishment of rights (EP.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Re‑establishment of rights may be requested where the applicant lost any right because, despite all due care required by the circumstances having been taken, he was unable to observe a time limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application for re‑establishment must be filed in writing within two months from removal of the cause of non‑compliance but not later than one year from expiration of the time limit. Within the two months the omitted act(s) must be completed, fees for re‑establishment paid and the request must state grounds and facts. Re‑establishment is ruled out where further processing is available (see Guidelines E‑IX, 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority documents: submission and consequences of omission (EP.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where priority of an earlier application is claimed the priority document is sent by the IB to the EPO if the IB received it from the receiving Office or directly from the applicant or could retrieve it from a digital library. The EPO will include free of charge in the file a copy retrievable via DAS when requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the priority document has not been submitted by entry into the national phase the applicant will be invited to furnish the missing document(s) within two months from the date of a notification under EPC Rule 163(2); this time limit cannot be extended. Failure to submit results in loss of the priority right, which may be remedied by requesting further processing. A priority document may be filed electronically with the EPO only if digitally signed by the issuing authority and the signature is accepted by the EPO; it cannot be filed by fax or Web‑Form Filing. For Euro‑PCT applications entering the European phase on or after 1 January 2022 the EPO discontinues free inclusion of certain PDX documents from US/Korean/Chinese offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of priority (EP.28)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the international application was filed more than 12 months from the filing date of the earlier application whose priority is claimed, the applicant may file or resubmit a request for restoration of priority under PCT Rule 49ter.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements include: the filing date is within two months from the date on which the priority period expired; the failure to claim priority occurred despite all due care; the request is filed within one month from the date the European phase expired for entry (or within one month from receipt of a request for early processing); the fee for restoration is paid within the same time limit; and the request is accompanied by a statement of reasons and preferably supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of entitlement to claim priority / successor in title (EP.29)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant claiming priority from a previous application must be the applicant of the latter or the successor in title. If the previous application was filed by several applicants, all applicants of the previous application must be applicants for the international application or must have transferred their rights to the applicant (or at least one of the applicants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If transfer took place, it must have occurred before the filing date of the international application and be valid under applicable national law. Proof of entitlement must be submitted in proceedings before the EPO only if validity of the priority right becomes relevant, but transfers required to be effective before the international filing date cannot be remedied in the national phase; applicants are strongly advised to ensure transfers are valid by the international filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of unity handling (EP.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: If documents serving as the basis for the supplementary European search or for examination contain claims to an invention not searched and do not meet the requirement of unity of invention, the procedure under EPC Rule 164 applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the EPO did not act as (S)ISA it draws up a partial supplementary European search report on the parts relating to the first mentioned invention and informs the applicant that coverage of other inventions requires payment of a further search fee within two months. If the EPO acted as (S)ISA and supplementary search was dispensed, the examining division will inform the applicant that a search will be performed for any such invention for which a search fee is paid within two months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference of correct elements (PCT Rule 20.5bis(d)) (EP.31)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the international phase it is possible to incorporate by reference correct elements or parts into the application as originally filed without changing the international filing date under PCT Rule 20.5bis(d), provided that rule's requirements are fulfilled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, incorporation allowed by the receiving Office will not be effective before the EPO due to incompatibility with the EPC. Applicants may inform the EPO within the 31‑month limit (or before the relevant communication) whether they wish to pursue the application on documents containing the correct elements with filing date changed to the date of receipt, or on the documents as originally filed (in which case the incorporated elements are disregarded). If no information is provided the EPO will send a communication under PCT Rule 20.8(c) and Rule 82ter.1(c) and (d) to clarify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees schedule and payment rules (Annex EP.I and Rules Relating to Fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: A detailed schedule of fees applies (filing fees for online and non‑online filings; additional fees for pages in excess of 35; divisional application fees by generation; designation, extension and validation fees; claims fees for the 16th/51st claims; search fee distinctions; examination fee differences; renewal fees per year; fees for further processing, late furnishing of sequence listings, grant/printing/publication; fees for re‑establishment and appeals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees are payable in euro by payment or transfer to a bank account held by the Office (Article 5). The President may allow other payment methods. Every payment must indicate the name of the person making the payment and contain necessary particulars to enable the Office to establish immediately the purpose of the payment (Article 6). Amounts and conditions are listed in Annex EP.I and in the Schedule of fees and expenses of the EPO; see Guidance for the payment of fees and expenses for current values.
